newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends up 25 cts, Aug Brent at $18.05.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends up 25 cts, Aug Brent at $18.05.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed 25 cents higher on Friday in quiet business little affected by firmer Brent crude and U.S. markets, brokers said.
Front month August gas oil settled at $162 a tonne after moving in a range between the low of $151.25 and high of $162.25.
"It was pretty quiet and rangebound and never looked like breaking out of it. There was good selling up at $162 and buying down at $161.25," a broker said.
Gas oil was unaffected by a rally on NYMEX gasoline built on gains in the cash gasoline market in Houston.
August Brent futures were up nine cents at $18.05 a barrel, down from the high of $18.15 touched in mid-afternoon a the peak of a rally on NYMEX gasoline.
Front month August gasoline was at 59.15 cents a gallon, up 0.55 cent on the day but down from the high of 59.90.
The gasoline strength boosted NYMEX crude, which was at $19.31 a barrel after touching a high of $19.44.
Volume in London remained very thin as dealers awaited a meeting on Sunday between the U.N. Iraq coordinator and Iraqi officials for more talks on Baghdad's aid distribution plan.
Prices fell sharply on Thursday when the German government said it planned to sell oil from its reserves in order to qualify for Europe's single currency.
Bonn said on Friday it would sell 2.8 million barrels of oil in the next few weeks and dispose of its entire strategic reserves of 7.3 million tonnes of crude oil.
